findings.finding: The safety fact: nothing outside tools/skills imports the new modules, and Jest already discovers tools/__tests__/*.test.js, so test:verified runs the new test without a config change. verify:commit at the head proves it.
findings.none: No breakage found; no existing caller changes.

findings.finding: Second author pass, looking past grep at the diff wire format: an added line whose text starts with "++ " prints as "+++ ..." in the --unified=0 diff, and parseAddedLines took it for a file header. The real file then lost its later added lines, so addedLines rules such as network-calls and credential-lines missed it. The header-lookalike test failed before the fix with network-care missing.
printRequired wrapped the skill id in a template literal that added nothing.
requiredSkills carried a comment that restated its name.
parseNumstat keeps one comment on the empty rename path, which is git numstat -z format that the code cannot show.
findings.none: Kept: it explains an external format.

findings.finding: Second author pass: the skill's first step spawns comment-sicko, and this pass runs without subagents, so I audited the comments inline. The two comments in change.cjs describe git output formats, the numstat rename fields and the tab after a spaced path.
findings.none: Kept both. They explain external formats that the code cannot show.

findings.finding: Routing JSON was parsed at the boundary but globs and patterns were rebuilt for every file inside the matcher.
network-calls and credential-lines matched routing.json, which holds their own pattern text.

Root cause of the change-rule bug: changeMatch modeled its filters as early returns, so the first filter decided the result. The fix makes the filters a conjunction instead of adding a special case for commitSubject.

Found in independent review: added-line rules never matched a path with a space, because git diff ends that "+++ b/" path with a tab. The new test failed with the skill missing, and passes after the tab is stripped. Paths that git still C-quotes, such as those with a tab or a double quote, are not handled.

Second author pass: the root cause of the header misread is that the parser had no state for where a file header ends. The fix reads headers only between "diff --git" and the first "@@" instead of filtering lookalike paths. A search of tools/ found no other diff parser with the same flaw.
cli.cjs dispatches four shapes of arguments in one if chain; each branch is one line, so a command table would add a layer without removing reading.

Seven code mutations (unsorted output, ignored exclusions, missed CommonJS exports, old rename path, plan content rules, missing root check, change filters not ANDed) each failed the fixture test; logs are in the PR evidence.
The rename mutation survived the first fixture, so the plan case gained a rename out of src/ before the feature commit.
routing.cjs exported a globs schema that nothing imported.
Second author pass: routing.cjs still exported matchesAny and change.cjs exported exportNames, and nothing in the stack imports either. The earlier pass removed one unused export but not the pattern.
The fixture test compares the exact printed output, which is the contract (deterministic, sorted, with every reason), and each mutation above changed that output.
docs/skills.md said a change rule tests one filter after the fix made filters a conjunction.
The committed-routing test asserts only that rules exist, but its protection is that parseRouting does not throw on a typo in a skill id.
findings.none: Kept: it is the only check of the real routing file.

findings.finding: Second author pass: the header-lookalike case shares the spaced-path test body through test.each, so both parse hazards run the real CLI and assert the full printed output. It failed before the fix with network-care missing for src/client.ts.
Change-rule filters were not composed like file-rule filters, which made the two rule kinds read differently.
No file passes 300 lines; routing, change reading, and the CLI each own one concern.
